name: Iron Belt trail, Zamudio (Berreaga–Gaztelumendi ridge)
story: Zamudio lies directly below the stretch of the Iron Belt where the Nationalists broke through. The fighting of 11–13 June 1937 spread along the Berreaga–Urrusti–Gaztelumendi ridge, and on 12 June the attackers crossed the line and came down into Zamudio. A signposted 11.1 km memory trail, marked with support from Gogora (the Basque Institute for Memory, Coexistence and Human Rights), climbs to the ridge past surviving trenches and machine-gun nests. It is one of the best places to understand what the Iron Belt actually looked like on the ground, and why it failed against massed artillery and aircraft.
see: Original trenches and concrete machine-gun posts along the ridge, with explanatory panels and waymarks.
plan: Start from the panel at the Arroeta car park in Zamudio. The 11 km loop takes about 4 h and is hilly; wear walking boots.
